one_sentence: This document argues that wavefunction collapse and the Fall of Genesis 3 share a five-property structural isomorphism, not merely an analogy.
executive_summary: This document establishes a five-property structural isomorphism between wavefunction collapse in quantum mechanics and the Fall in Genesis 3. It maps five defining properties of collapse—instantaneous, irreversible, non-local, regime-changing, and information-gaining at the cost of freedom—onto five corresponding properties of the Fall. The mapping is bidirectional, with each domain predicting and constraining the other. The conclusion is that both events are manifestations of the same underlying substrate operating at different scales, one physical and one moral. The document includes separability tests and kill conditions to ensure the isomorphism is falsifiable.
short_summary: This document is a formal isomorphism paper mapping wavefunction collapse to the Fall of Genesis 3. The core structural claim is that five properties of quantum collapse—instantaneous, irreversible, non-local, regime-changing, and information-gaining—map one-to-one onto five properties of the Fall. Key evidence includes the Hebrew grammar of Genesis 3:7, the cherubim barrier in Genesis 3:24, and Bell's theorem confirming non-locality. This matters because it suggests a unified substrate underlying physical and moral reality, with testable predictions for both domains.
